title: NDJSON continuation tokens and toolcall idempotency for streaming structured outputs
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: Customers experience corrupt or partially-applied structured outputs when a streaming response is truncated mid-object or when tool/function calls interleave with JSON lines. Existing heuristics (heuristic reassembly and fragment sentinels) have reduced incidents but are brittle across heterogeneous SDK clients. Goal: Define a pragmatic NDJSON continuation protocol and toolcall idempotency contract that (1) minimizes breaking changes to SDKs, (2) improves recoverability on truncation or partial delivery, (3) enables safe retry semantics for tool/function invocations, and (4) provides a compact on-the-wire footprint for low-latency streaming.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits NDJSON where each line is a JSON object with an optional continuation_token field when the line is a partial object
Tool/function call blocks include an idempotency_key and a call_seq integer to allow exact replay and deduplication on retry
Client SDKs can resume a stream given the last successfully-parsed line and the latest continuation_token without requiring full-object reassembly heuristics
There is a documented backoff and retry policy for clients and a guidance page in Console docs

Integration tests that simulate mid-object truncation, multi-call interleaving, and reconnect-based resumption show no spurious duplicate tool-side effects when idempotency_key and call_seq are honored
proposed_solution: Protocol summary: 1) Line framing: stream uses NDJSON (newline-delimited JSON). Each emitted JSON object is either a complete record OR a fragment. 2) Continuation token: fragments include continuation_token (string) and fragment_index (int). The final fragment of an object omits continuation_token. 3) Checksum: each line carries a short sha1_prefix (8 hex chars) to detect corruption; clients validate and request resume if checksum mismatches. 4) Toolcall envelope: when the model requests a tool/function, it emits a tool_call object with required fields: name, args, idempotency_key (UUIDv4), call_seq (monotonic integer per-stream). 5) Retry semantics: client may retry to the server with resume_token (the last continuation_token) and the last-acknowledged call_seq. Server must dedupe tool calls by idempotency_key and preserve ordering by call_seq. 6) Truncation handling: when connection closes mid-fragment the client reopens with resume_token and indicates last_parsed_line_checksum; server responds with a small re-transmit window (configurable) starting at earliest matching fragment_index. 7) Graceful degrade: if resume not possible, fall back to delivering an object with partial=true and truncated=true metadata along with a human-readable warning and a recommended next-action (retry or escalate).
implementation_notes: Add continuation_token, fragment_index, and sha1_prefix fields to server streaming NDJSON emitter (backwards-compatible: servers can omit continuation_token for single-line objects)
Extend toolcall codepath to require idempotency_key and call_seq; validate uniqueness server-side and persist minimal call metadata (idempotency_key -> result/status) for 24h
Add resume endpoint param: resume_token + last_parsed_line_checksum + last_ack_call_seq

SDK changes: streaming parser should operate line-by-line, validate sha1_prefix, reassemble fragments in memory keyed by continuation_token, and expose a resumable stream API (resume() taking server resume reply)
Add end-to-end tests: simulated packet loss mid-line, truncated TCP streams, and simultaneous toolcall replay across reconnects
Update Console docs and examples showing error codes for RESUME_REQUIRED, CHECKSUM_MISMATCH, and CALL_IDEMPOTENCY_VIOLATION
open_questions: Should continuation_token be opaque (recommended) or include a version/prefix to support future format changes?
What retention window for idempotency metadata balances storage cost and customer safety? 24h default but maybe configurable per-customer
Do we need server-side signed resume_tokens to prevent clients from requesting arbitrary offsets?
How will this interact with Dedicated/private deployments where local network proxies may buffer and alter newline semantics?
Should we include an optional human_readable_fragment_hint to help low-fi clients present partial content?
